newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian paper shows first post-op photo of Yeltsin.
newsitem.headline: Russian paper shows first post-op photo of Yeltsin.

text.p: A Russian newspaper on Saturday published the first picture of President Boris Yeltsin since he underwent open heart surgery 11 days ago.
The photograph, taking up much of the front page of the liberal daily Sevodnya, showed a relaxed-looking Yeltsin drinking tea with his wife Naina and granddaugher Masha.
Yeltsin was wearing an open-necked shirt and a patterned cardigan.

Sevodnya said the photograph, released by the presidential press service, was taken on Friday at the presidential section of the Central Clinical Hospital, where the president is recuperating from a quintuple bypass operation.

The president has just completed the first 100 days of his second term in office, but his heart problems meant he spent only a handful of days in the Kremlin. Doctors say the operation appears to have been a success and Yeltsin is recovering well.
The picture seemed to be the latest step in the Kremlin's strategy of gradually preparing the 65-year-old president for a full public appearance.
On Friday his press secretary Sergei Yastrzhembsky said a planned address to the nation, Yeltsin's first public act, was still being prepared. But he did not say when it would be.
Yastrzhembsky had said on Tuesday that Yeltsin would address the nation within days, but did not specify whether this would be on television or radio.
On Friday the press spokesman said no timetable for an address had been laid down and added: "You understand, the imagemakers want the president's appearance to have a big impact."

In a regular health bulletin released on Friday, Yeltsin's doctors said the president's condition remained "completely satisfactory", with a steady pulse of 70 to 82 beats a minute and normal temperature and blood pressure.
They said he spent three hours working on official papers on Friday.
